chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Faddala, from Aban, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who kills a snake. The questioner said to him: 'It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: He who leaves it out of fear of its consequence is not from me.' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: And he who leaves it out of fear of its consequence is not from me.' As for a snake that does not seek you, there is no harm in leaving it.

key_terms.تَبِعَتِهَا: consequence or effect (of the snake's bite)
key_terms.لَا تَطْلُبُكَ: does not seek you (i.e., is not aggressive)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on killing snakes according to the Prophet's tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to resolve the apparent contradiction in prophetic traditions regarding snakes by distinguishing between aggressive threats and passive coexistence. The Imam clarifies that the warning 'he is not from me' specifically targets those who leave a snake out of mere precaution or fear of its bite, whereas snakes that do not actively seek you out or cause harm should be left alone. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on contextual interpretation (ta'wil) of hadith, balancing the Prophet's authority with practical natural behavior.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Khalid, from his father, from Faddala, from Aban, that he said:

Abu’l-Hasan, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who kills a snake, and the questioner said to him: Indeed, it has reached us that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: «The one who leaves it out of precaution from its consequences, then he is not from me». He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: «And the one who leaves it out of precaution from its consequences, then he is not from me». As for a snake [1] that does not seek you, there is no harm in leaving it.
